## data

### Components (data)

#### TradingDataProvider

*component* · [data/TradingDataProvider.tsx](../../packages/trading-ui/src/data/TradingDataProvider.tsx#L86)

Selects the data source implementation for every trading component below
it. Components never construct data sources directly: they call
useTradingDataSource (or useData().VuuDataSource), so the same component
runs against the portal's server, a standalone server or local test data.

Props: `TradingDataProviderProps`

One of:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `mode` | `"inherit"` |  | Use the enclosing |

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `mode` | `"local"` |  | In-browser data. |
| `localServer` | `LocalVuuServer` |  | e.g. `createTradingLocalServer()` from |

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `mode` | `"remote"` |  | A Vuu server connection. |
| `connectionId` | `string` |  | The id passed to connectToVuuServer / ConnectionManager.connectTo. |

### Hooks (data)

#### useChartDataSource

*hook* · [data/useChartDataSource.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/data/useChartDataSource.ts#L31)

A DataSource dedicated to one vuu-chart (or one chart overlay).

vuu-chart subscribes with no filter or sort of its own and *unsubscribes*
its DataSources on unmount or when a DataSource prop changes, so charts
must never share a DataSource with a table or another chart. This hook
creates a fresh DataSource whenever table, filter, sort or columns change,
with the filter and sort applied server-side (charts only read the first
`maxRows` rows). Unsubscribing is left to the chart.

```ts
useChartDataSource(table: TradingSchemaName, { columns, disabled = false, filter, sort }: ChartDataSourceOptions = {}): DataSource | undefined
```

#### useDataSourceRows

*hook* · [data/useDataSourceRows.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/data/useDataSourceRows.ts#L228)

Rows of a data source you own (from useTradingDataSource, not one a vuu
Table drives) as objects, for custom renderers (depth, ladder, tape) and
headless logic. Subscribed while `enabled`; re-subscribed - with the rows
cleared at once, so an instrument switch never shows stale rows - when
`filter`, `groupBy`, `aggregations` or the range change; unsubscribed on
unmount. Bursts of updates cost one render per animation frame.

```ts
useDataSourceRows<T extends TradingRow = TradingRow>(dataSource: DataSource | undefined, { enabled = true, throttle = "frame", ...config }: UseDataSourceRowsOptions = {}): DataSourceRows<T>
```

#### useHasDataProvider

*hook* · [data/TradingDataProvider.tsx](../../packages/trading-ui/src/data/TradingDataProvider.tsx#L117)

True when a data provider is available (outside one, data sources fail).

```ts
useHasDataProvider(): boolean
```

#### useTableSelectedKeys

*hook* · [data/useTableSelectedKeys.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/data/useTableSelectedKeys.ts#L59)

Track which row keys a vuu Table has selected. The Table reports selection
as requests (`onSelectionChange`), not row sets; this folds them into a Set
of keys. Pass the Table's `onSelectionChange`. `orderedKeys` is only needed
for range / select-all.

```ts
useTableSelectedKeys(orderedKeys: readonly string[]): { selectedKeys: ReadonlySet<string>; onSelectionChange: SelectionChangeHandler; clear: () => void; }
```

#### useTradingDataMode

*hook* · [data/TradingDataProvider.tsx](../../packages/trading-ui/src/data/TradingDataProvider.tsx#L45)

The active TradingDataProvider mode (`inherit` without a provider).

```ts
useTradingDataMode(): TradingDataModeContextValue
```

#### useTradingDataSource

*hook* · [data/useTradingDataSource.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/data/useTradingDataSource.ts#L25)

A DataSource for a trading table from the nearest data provider (local
test data, remote server or portal host - see TradingDataProvider).

`options` (columns, sort, filterSpec, groupBy, aggregations, ...) are
initial config only: the data source is created once per table/provider.
Change config afterwards through the DataSource (`ds.sort = ...`) or let
a vuu Table drive it. Columns default to every column of the schema.
The data source is unsubscribed on unmount.

```ts
useTradingDataSource(table: TradingSchemaName, options: TradingDataSourceOptions = {}): DataSource
```

#### useTradingRows

*hook* · [data/useTradingRows.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/data/useTradingRows.ts#L32)

useTradingDataSource + useDataSourceRows in one call: the rows of a
trading table (first `rowCount`, default 100) as objects, kept up to date.
`filter` (default: none), `groupBy`, `aggregations`, `enabled` and
`throttle` behave as in useDataSourceRows (updates are frame-coalesced
unless `throttle: "none"`);
other options (columns, sort, ...) are initial data source config.


#### connectToVuuServer

*function* · [data/connectToVuuServer.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/data/connectToVuuServer.ts#L138)

Authenticate against a vuu-server REST auth endpoint (permissive auth in

with ConnectionManager. Resolves once connected; rejects on auth or
connection failure (or no LOGIN answer within `loginTimeoutMs`).

Once connected, a ReconnectSupervisor reconnects after the socket drops
(`reconnect`), publishing reconnecting / failed for the status hooks.

Inside vuu-portal the host does this - features use mode="inherit".

#### sendTradingRpc

*function* · [data/tradingRpc.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/data/tradingRpc.ts#L107)

Send a typed trading RPC (createOrder, amendOrder, cancelOrder, cancelAll,
exchange admin) through a data source of the owning module (OMS for order
RPCs, EXCHANGE for admin). The data source adds the viewport context, so
it must be subscribed (e.g. rendered by a Table). Resolves with the response
data, rejects with TradingRpcError: a server reject, or (`transport`) not
sent because `connectionState` is not "connected", or no answer within
`timeoutMs` (default DEFAULT_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS).

```ts
sendTradingRpc<N extends RpcName>(dataSource: DataSource, rpcName: N, params: RpcRequestParams<N>, { timeoutMs = DEFAULT_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS, connectionState, }: TradingRpcOptions = {}): Promise<RpcResponseData<N>>
```

### Functions (instrument-context)

#### bindInstrumentLinkStore

*function* · [instrument-context/instrumentLinkPersistence.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/instrument-context/instrumentLinkPersistence.ts#L93)

Keep the selections of the bus's shared link groups in `store`, so they
survive a reload. Once the store is loaded, saved selections fill the
groups that have none yet (a popout that already synced over
BroadcastChannel keeps what it got). Every later change is saved; changes
saved by another window are applied last-writer-wins (by seq), like
BroadcastChannel messages. Clearing the document in the Saved state
dialog clears the selections. Returns unbind.

```ts
bindInstrumentLinkStore(bus: InstrumentLinkBus, store: InstrumentLinkStateStore): (() => void)
```

#### connectBroadcastChannel

*function* · [instrument-context/broadcastChannelTransport.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/instrument-context/broadcastChannelTransport.ts#L53)

Link the bus with the same-named bus of other windows / tabs of the same
origin (popouts, multi-monitor). Local selections of shared groups are
posted; received ones are applied last-writer-wins and never re-posted,
so there are no loops. A new window asks for the current selections.
Returns disconnect. A no-op where BroadcastChannel is unavailable.

```ts
connectBroadcastChannel(bus: InstrumentLinkBus, { name = DEFAULT_LINK_CHANNEL_NAME, channel, }: ConnectBroadcastChannelOptions = {}): (() => void)
```

#### InstrumentLinkBus

*interface* · [instrument-context/instrumentLinkBus.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/instrument-context/instrumentLinkBus.ts#L39)

A framework-free pub/sub of the selected instrument per link group.
One instance is shared by everything in a window (getInstrumentLinkBus),
so separately mounted MF features that do not share a React tree still
link; transports (BroadcastChannel) extend it to other windows.

| Member | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` |  | Unique per bus instance; the `origin` of its own selections. |
| `version` | `number` |  | Protocol version of this bus (see INSTRUMENT_LINK_BUS_VERSION). |
| `getSelection` | `(group: LinkGroupId) => InstrumentLinkSelection \| undefined` |  |  |
| `publish` | `(group: LinkGroupId, instrument: SelectedInstrument \| undefined, source?: string) => boolean` |  | Select `instrument` (or clear with undefined) in `group`. The value is reduced to plain SelectedInstrument fields. Returns false (and notifies nobody) when nothing changes: the same ric with no new static data, a missing / blank ric, or the bare `unlinked` group. |
| `subscribe` | `(group: LinkGroupId, listener: InstrumentLinkListener) => () => void` |  | Listen to one group. Returns unsubscribe. |
| `subscribeAll` | `(listener: InstrumentLinkListener) => () => void` |  | Listen to every group (bridges, logging). Returns unsubscribe. |
| `receive` | `(group: LinkGroupId, selection: InstrumentLinkSelection) => boolean` |  | Apply a selection made on another bus. Ignored if it is our own, older than the current one (last writer wins by seq, then origin) or private. |
| `snapshot` | `() => [LinkGroupId, InstrumentLinkSelection][]` |  | Current selections of the shared (not private) groups. |
| `addTransport` | `(transport: InstrumentLinkTransport) => () => void` |  | Forward local selections of shared groups. Returns remove. |
| `clear` | `() => void` |  | Forget all selections (no notification). For tests / sign-out. |

## hooks

### Hooks (hooks)

#### useBookQueue

*hook* · [hooks/useBookQueue.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/hooks/useBookQueue.ts#L140)

The order-by-order (L3) queue of every price level of one instrument,
from EXCHANGE `bookOrders`, with the user's orders marked. The table is
empty when the server runs with `exchangeSim.bookOrders=0`.

```ts
useBookQueue(ric: string | undefined, { enabled = true, ownOrderIds, maxOrders = 2_000 }: BookQueueOptions = {}): BookQueueState
```

#### useFollowedInstrument

*hook* · [hooks/useMarketData.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/hooks/useMarketData.ts#L190)

The instrument a market-data component shows: the explicit `ric` prop
when given, else the selected instrument of the link group
(useSelectedInstrument), with its live instrumentPrices row. Rics with no
reference data still resolve (`{ ric }` until / unless prices arrive).

```ts
useFollowedInstrument(ricOverride?: string, { linkGroup }: { linkGroup?: LinkGroupId } = {}): FollowedInstrument
```

#### useInstrumentPrice

*hook* · [hooks/useMarketData.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/hooks/useMarketData.ts#L89)

The `instrumentPrices` row of one instrument (static data plus live
bid/ask/last/phase), or undefined until it arrives.

```ts
useInstrumentPrice(ric: string | undefined): InstrumentPrice | undefined
```

#### useLevelFlash

*hook* · [hooks/useLevelFlash.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/hooks/useLevelFlash.ts#L18)

Detect quantity changes per (side, price) between depth updates. Returns
flashes for the levels that changed in the latest update. Idempotent per
`version`, so StrictMode double renders don't swallow flashes. Resets
when `resetKey` (e.g. the ric) changes, so a switch doesn't flash.

```ts
useLevelFlash(levels: readonly DepthLevel[], version: number, resetKey: unknown): Map<string, LevelFlash>
```

#### useMarketDepth

*hook* · [hooks/useMarketData.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/hooks/useMarketData.ts#L43)

The aggregated book (EXCHANGE `depth`) for one instrument, split into
bids and asks, best first. `levels` caps the levels per side (the table
carries `exchangeSim.depthLevels`, 10 by default). Rows of a previous
`ric` are never returned.

```ts
useMarketDepth(ric: string | undefined, { levels = 10 }: { levels?: number } = {}): MarketDepthState
```

#### useOrderBook

*hook* · [hooks/useOrderBook.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/hooks/useOrderBook.ts#L150)

One parent order with the book it is working in: its child orders, the
instrument's L2 depth (EXCHANGE `depth`) and L3 queues (EXCHANGE
`bookOrders`), the working child orders marked with their queue position.
Subscribes only while `orderId` is set.

```ts
useOrderBook(orderId: string | undefined, { levels = 10 }: OrderBookOptions = {}): OrderBookState
```

#### useOwnExchangeOrderIds

*hook* · [hooks/useOwnExchangeOrderIds.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/hooks/useOwnExchangeOrderIds.ts#L14)

Exchange order ids (OMS `childOrders.exchangeOrderId`) of the working
child orders of `orders`, so the user's orders can be picked out of the
anonymous L3 book (`bookOrders.orderId`).

```ts
useOwnExchangeOrderIds(ric: string | undefined, orders: readonly OwnOrder[], { enabled = true, maxOrders = 1_000 } = {}): ReadonlySet<string>
```

#### useOwnWorkingOrders

*hook* · [hooks/useOwnWorkingOrders.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/hooks/useOwnWorkingOrders.ts#L97)

Working LIMIT orders, and STOP_LIMIT orders once triggered (OMS
`parentOrders`, visible to the current user) for one instrument, also
aggregated by side and price. Used for own-order
markers in depth views and the price ladder. The OMS only returns orders
the user is entitled to see (see oms README, permissions).

```ts
useOwnWorkingOrders(ric: string | undefined, { account, maxOrders = 500 }: OwnWorkingOrdersOptions = {}): OwnWorkingOrders
```

#### useStableCallback

#### createResilientConnectionRegistry

*function* · [connection/resilientConnectionRegistry.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/connection/resilientConnectionRegistry.ts#L206)

A VuuConnectionRegistry for a portal host (AuthenticationProvider

by default, never gives up (vuu-ui's default schedule is 1-120 s without
jitter and stops after ~4 minutes, then fails the module or the whole
portal: trader upstream issue 84). Each connect attempt has a timeout
(trader upstream issue 83). Its state is observed for
useTradingConnectionStatus.

```ts

```

#### withConnectTimeout

*function* · [connection/resilientConnectionRegistry.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/connection/resilientConnectionRegistry.ts#L54)

Reject a connect attempt that does not settle within `timeoutMs`.

Trader upstream issue 83: when vuu-server refuses a LOGIN with a text
frame vuu-ui does not recognise (e.g. "maximum sessions (5) reached for
user alice", "Invalid session <id>"), the worker never settles the
pending login, so ConnectionManager.connectWithLoginResponseTo never
resolves and VuuConnectionRegistry's reconnect loop stops for good.
With the timeout the attempt fails and the loop tries again later.

```ts
withConnectTimeout<T>(attempt: Promise<T>, connectionId: string, timeoutMs = DEFAULT_LOGIN_TIMEOUT_MS): Promise<T>
```

#### ReconnectSupervisor

*class* · [connection/ReconnectSupervisor.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/connection/ReconnectSupervisor.ts#L65)

The reconnect state machine for a connection trader opens itself
(connectToVuuServer). Under the portal VuuConnectionRegistry owns the
loop instead (createResilientConnectionRegistry).

  idle --connected()--> connected --connectionLost()--> reconnecting
  reconnecting --attempt ok--> connected
  reconnecting --attempt failed--> reconnecting (backoff + jitter)
                               --maxAttempts reached--> failed
  failed --retryNow() / connectionLost()--> reconnecting
  any --stop()--> stopped (terminal)

Only one attempt runs at a time; connectionLost() while reconnecting is
ignored, so the socket's own "disconnected" events during an attempt do
not multiply attempts.

```ts
new ReconnectSupervisor({ connect, onChange, policy, random = Math.random, timers = defaultTimers, }: ReconnectSupervisorOptions)
```

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `state` |  |
| `snapshot` |  |
| `connected()` | The connection is up (initial connect, or established elsewhere). |
| `connectionLost(error?: unknown)` | The socket dropped: start a reconnect episode unless one is running. |
| `retryNow()` | Attempt now (e.g. a "Retry now" button), skipping the backoff. |
| `stop()` |  |

#### ReconnectPolicy

*interface* · [connection/reconnectPolicy.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/connection/reconnectPolicy.ts#L6)

Reconnect backoff: exponential, capped, with jitter so that many tabs
(or many users) dropped by the same server restart do not all reconnect
in the same instant (docs/resilience.md).

| Member | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `initialDelayMs?` | `number` |  | Delay before the first attempt (ms). Default 1000. |
| `maxDelayMs?` | `number` |  | Upper bound for any delay (ms). Default 30000. |
| `multiplier?` | `number` |  | Growth factor per attempt. Default 2. |
| `jitter?` | `number` |  | Fraction of each delay that is randomised, 0..1. A delay `d` becomes a value in `[d * (1 - jitter), d]`. Default 0.5. |
| `maxAttempts?` | `number` |  | Give up after this many failed attempts. Default Infinity (never). |

and expiries of the user's orders, from the parentOrders / fills streams

#### NotificationGate

*class* · [notifications/NotificationGate.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/notifications/NotificationGate.ts#L44)

Dedupe + rate limiting for notifications. The same event can arrive from

streams; bursts (cancelAll, a sweep filling many orders) collapse into a

## feature-root

### Components (feature-root)

#### TradingFeatureRoot

*component* · [feature-root/TradingFeatureRoot.tsx](../../packages/trading-ui/src/feature-root/TradingFeatureRoot.tsx#L79)

What every trading MF feature wraps its content in. It mounts the
per-host services once:

- Nested in another TradingFeatureRoot (a composite feature rendering
  child modules): renders children only.
- Otherwise: TradingNotificationsProvider (with InstrumentLookupProvider),
  OrderTicketLauncherProvider and ConnectionBanner. Only one root per
  window streams order notifications (window-global lease), so several
  features open in one portal do not toast each event twice.
- Always: the window link bus is connected to BroadcastChannel once, so
  popped-out features stay linked, and saved in the portal's persistence
  service once, so channel selections survive a reload.

The vuu NotificationsProvider (toast centre) is the host's: vuu-portal
mounts it. Data comes from the enclosing DataProvider (mode "inherit").

Props: `TradingFeatureRootProps`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `connectionBanner?` | `boolean` | `true` | Render the ConnectionBanner (default true). |
| `notifications?` | `boolean` | `true` | Stream order notifications if no other root in the window does (default true). |
| `scope?` | `"trader" \| "visibleAccounts"` |  | "trader" (default): the trader's own orders. "visibleAccounts": every order on accounts the user can see (supervisors). (from `TradingNotificationsProviderProps`) |
| `kinds?` | `Partial<TradingNotificationKinds>` |  | Initial per-kind settings (merged with the defaults). (from `TradingNotificationsProviderProps`) |

(or prices). Price-move and change renderers, formatting per instrument,
grouping, column picker, quick filter, watchlists, phase badge, optional

grid (`followSelection`).

## components/OrderTicket

### Components (components/OrderTicket)

#### OrderTicket

*component* · [components/OrderTicket/OrderTicket.tsx](../../packages/trading-ui/src/components/OrderTicket/OrderTicket.tsx#L1114)

Order entry. The side buttons carry the quote (Sell on the bid, Buy on
the ask). Instrument, side, quantity and price stay in place; the
execution strategy and its parameters (from the strategy definitions)
sit below them. Keyboard first:
- Tab: instrument → quantity → (stop) → price → strategy → its fields →
  send.
- Alt / Option + B / S side; L limit, M market, P stop, Shift+P stop
  limit; T next TIF; E strategy.
- Enter accepts a field and moves on; Ctrl+Enter or F9 sends.
- Price `b` / `a` / `m` / `b+2`; quantity `10k` / `$250k`.
- The instrument field takes a whole order line (`b 5k vod.l b twap 45m`,
  `s 200 vod.l stop 99.5 lmt 99.4`).
Orders over a limit or outside the collar go through Review first.

Props: `OrderTicketProps`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant?` | `OrderTicketVariant` | `"panel"` | "panel" (default): full form for a docked panel or dialog. "compact": a one-line strip for a grid row or ladder. |
| `showInstrumentPicker?` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the instrument picker (default true; false for a fixed ric). |
| `actions?` | `ReactNode` |  | Extra content in the actions row (e.g. a Close button). |

#### parseOrderLine

*function* · [components/OrderTicket/orderTicketModel.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/components/OrderTicket/orderTicketModel.ts#L884)

Parse an order typed as one line, e.g. `b 20k aal.l m vwap 15:30`:
side (first word, `b` / `s`), quantity (first number), instrument (a word
with a dot), price (a later number or `b` / `a` / `m`, `mkt` for market),
strategy (by id or name) and its parameters (by their form: `45m`,
`15:30`, `10%`). Words may come in any order after the side, except that
quantity comes before price. Missing parts are left as they are.

Stops: `stop` (or `stp`) takes the next price as the stop price; with a
limit price as well the order is a STOP_LIMIT, e.g. `s 200 vod.l stop
99.5` (STOP) and `s 200 vod.l stop 99.5 lmt 99.4` (STOP_LIMIT). `lmt`
(`limit`) before a price is optional: any other price is the limit.

```ts
parseOrderLine(text: string): OrderLine
```

#### PriceLadder

*component* · [components/PriceLadder/PriceLadder.tsx](../../packages/trading-ui/src/components/PriceLadder/PriceLadder.tsx#L195)

Price ladder (depth of market) bound to live data: EXCHANGE depth,
instrumentPrices and (optionally) trades for the selected instrument (or
`ric`), plus the user's working orders from the OMS. Click-to-trade sends
`createOrder` (LIMIT, own clOrdId); dragging own orders sends
`amendOrder`; Delete / double-click sends `cancelOrder`; Cancel all sends
`cancelAll`. Results are reported through `onOrderEvent` / `onError`.

#### PriceLadderView

*component* · [components/PriceLadder/PriceLadderView.tsx](../../packages/trading-ui/src/components/PriceLadder/PriceLadderView.tsx#L667)

Presentational price ladder (DOM): one row per tick around a centre price;
columns own bids | bid qty | price | ask qty | own offers (| volume).
Holds the UI state (centre, cursor, auto-centre, confirm, drag) and emits
intents (`onTrade`, `onAmendOrders`, `onCancelOrders`, `onCancelAll`).
Rows are recycled by slot and memoised, so an update re-renders only rows
whose values changed. `PriceLadder` binds it to live data and RPCs.

#### Sparkline

*component* · [components/Sparkline/Sparkline.tsx](../../packages/trading-ui/src/components/Sparkline/Sparkline.tsx#L48)

Props: `SparklineProps`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |

Also accepts the standard SVG attributes and `ref`.

#### SparklineCell

*component* · [components/Sparkline/Sparkline.tsx](../../packages/trading-ui/src/components/Sparkline/Sparkline.tsx#L160)

Table cell renderer `trading.sparkline`.

Keeps a client-side ring buffer per row (see `sparklineStore`), appends the
row's `valueColumn` on every change and redraws by updating the polyline
directly: no React re-render per tick beyond the Table's own cell update.
The buffer is released when the row's cell unmounts or is recycled for
another row. History therefore only accumulates while a row is in the
viewport, as the server only streams visible rows.

Use with a client column (not in the server schema):
`{ name: "sparkline", source: "client", sortable: false, type: { name: "string",
   renderer: { name: "trading.sparkline", componentProps: { valueColumn: "last", length: 40 } } } }`

Props: `TableCellRendererProps`

Also accepts the props of `TableCellProps (@vuu-ui/vuu-table-types)`, `TableCellRendererProps (@vuu-ui/vuu-table-types)`.

Names of the generic trading cell renderers. Use them as a column
`type`:


They read sibling columns from the same row, so those columns must be in

have run; the components that use them call it.


#### TradingColour

*const* · [utils/colours.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/utils/colours.ts#L9)

Semantic colours as CSS custom properties. Each `--trading-*` token falls
back to a Salt token, so it follows the theme / mode by default and can be
overridden by an app (e.g. `.my-app { --trading-buy: teal }`).
Use the values in inline styles or CSS (`color: var(--trading-buy)`).

```ts
const TradingColour: Readonly<{ readonly buy: "var(--trading-buy, var(--salt-sentiment-positive-foreground-informative))"; readonly sell: "var(--trading-sell, var(--salt-sentiment-negative-foreground-informative))"; ... 7 more ...; readonly done: "var(--trading-status-done, var(--salt-content-secondary-foreground))"; }>
```

#### UserSettingsProviderProps

#### UserSettingsStorage

*interface* · [utils/userSettingsStorage.ts](../../packages/trading-ui/src/utils/userSettingsStorage.ts#L29)

Where components persist per-user settings (watchlists, layouts, ...).

The shape is deliberately a subset of the Web Storage API, so
`window.localStorage` is a valid implementation, but values may also be
returned asynchronously. A host with a real user-settings backend (for
example vuu-portal's user settings service) supplies its own implementation:

```ts
const portalSettings: UserSettingsStorage = {
  getItem: (key) => settingsApi.get(`trading/${key}`),   // Promise<string | null>
  setItem: (key, value) => settingsApi.put(`trading/${key}`, value),
  removeItem: (key) => settingsApi.delete(`trading/${key}`),
};
<UserSettingsProvider storage={portalSettings}>...</UserSettingsProvider>
```

Values are JSON strings; keys are namespaced by the component, e.g.
`trading.watchlists`.

| Member | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `getItem` | `(key: string) => string \| null \| undefined \| Promise<string \| null \| undefined>` |  |  |
| `setItem` | `(key: string, value: string) => void \| Promise<void>` |  |  |
| `removeItem?` | `(key: string) => void \| Promise<void>` |  |  |
